comments.author: @comewithit2952
comments.text: Also....the original argument for using UPS, FedEx, Amazon, was that it was cheaper to do so. NOW, the people working for those companies make a lot more than postal workers do. And they do not have to walk up and down splits in the city delivering mail to individualized boxes ///especially apartment buildings/// and just drop stop packages. SO...A lot of those other companies are just having the post office do the work instead. There are not less packages being shipped and delivered. Just WHO does it. More than 75% of the packages on my route now have USPS shipping labels but the boxes or plastic say the other companies.

comments.author: @comewithit2952
comments.text: I've been working for almost a year there. The main problem is that they can't predict what the mail volume is going to be day to day and shuffle people around based upon that. You are on your way to work at one post office and enroute get a call from them and are told to go to another one...2 hours later than you thought you wee going to work. This can go on for days, weeks, and so on. ALSO....they expect packages AND mail to be delivered together. SO...If you have a route one day with 35 packages and the next with 135 packages...they expect you to deliver in the same time for either.
